clue.text: All the same as an all-seater?

definitions.meaning: a stadium with every place a seat is read as '...' room

explanation.surface: A remark about stadium design, comparing an all-seater ground to something unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-seater stadium has no standing terraces, so it is 'not with standing'; split the word differently and it means 'nevertheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless and despite that are standard synonyms for the conjunction-like adverb.

clue.text: 49%? I couldn't agree more!

definitions.meaning: a little under 50 per cent is less than a half
British slang exclamation of emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: A statistic followed by a hearty exclamation of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang meaning 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short of half literally, and colloquially an emphatic British 'absolutely!'.

clue.text: Job taken up by skilled artisan

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A craftsman accepts a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'taken up' turns the letters EDART, from skilleD ARTisan, to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled occupation or line of work.

clue.text: Country Dane is in travelling round Odense, primarily

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other letter
travelling suggests the letters of Dane is in move about
primarily means take just the first letter of Odense

explanation.surface: A Danish tourist touring the city of Odense is in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges DANE IS IN, and 'round' wraps it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation of islands in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Drone, an English kind

parts.note: to drone is to make a continuous hum

explanation.surface: A type of male bee is described as English.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate, synonym of kind as an adjective.

clue.text: Terribly sore, but fine in the end admittedly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of sore but are badly mixed up
in the end means take just the closing letter of fine

explanation.surface: An injury hurts a lot but will heal eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase concedes a point, used like 'granted' or 'I admit'.

clue.text: Nothing to secure a tack

indicators.note: to secure means the zero word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: No fastening is used to fix a small pin.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack something down is to fix it, as with a hammer and pin.

clue.text: Enter reduction in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters of reduction are put down wrongly

explanation.surface: A mistaken cut is typed into a record.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a bill in parliament is to bring it in, put it forward.

clue.text: Italian wingers, certainly not tackled

indicators.note: tackled, as of birds grappling a word, means the refusal goes inside

parts.note: geese are winged birds, so wingers
no is a firm refusal

explanation.surface: Italy's wide players were never brought down in a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' looks like football but means birds; the answer is a person from Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Genoa, a city in north-west Italy, is an Italian.

clue.text: Smart criminal hosting party in realm of emperor

indicators.note: hosting means the jumbled letters hold the party word inside them
criminal suggests the letters of smart are bent out of their proper order

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A slick crook throws a party within an imperial kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as an adjective for the criminal, but it is the anagram fodder and 'criminal' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor, and the suffix -dom names the domain he rules.

clue.text: Sound of country music writer

indicators.note: sound of tells us to take a word that is said like the country

parts.note: Britain is the country meant

explanation.surface: Talk of a nation's country-and-western tunes and their songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was a twentieth-century English composer; 'country music' tempts as a genre but splits into country and music writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was an English composer, and a composer writes music.

clue.text: A writer figures they're mountains

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
nines are numerical figures

explanation.surface: An author is doing sums about some peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the spine of Italy.

clue.text: Shy of 135 degrees, this smells!

parts.note: being shy of something is lacking it, so no
a compass bearing of 135 degrees is south-east, SE

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: an angle just short of 135 degrees has a smell about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the compass: 135 degrees clockwise from north is south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is the organ a person or animal uses to sniff out odours.

clue.text: Polish European, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it asks for a word said just like the nationality

parts.note: a Finnish person comes from Finland in Europe

explanation.surface: Someone from Poland is mistaken for another European nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb, not the nationality; the European is Finnish.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish a piece of furniture is to give it a final gloss or surface treatment.

clue.text: Strangely right, a new pair of pyjamas, perhaps?

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of right a new form an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: Oddly enough, someone has new pyjamas that fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas are an example of clothes worn in bed.

clue.text: Old maid wrapping up nonsense project

indicators.note: wrapping up means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a prude, stereotypically a prim old maid
rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A spinster concludes a silly scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to stick out beyond a surface, as a ledge does.

clue.text: Counsellor this time admitting cut up

indicators.note: admitting means the word this lets the other piece inside
in a down answer, up means the trim word is read upward

parts.note: to pare is to cut

explanation.surface: An adviser is now taking in someone upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' suggests distress, but 'up' only turns the trimming word upward in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist offers counselling to clients.

clue.text: Page soon featuring the eminent group

indicators.note: featuring means the word anon includes the article inside

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A page will soon show the great and good.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the collection of a nation's or field's most revered figures.

clue.text: Keep scores holding a winter celebration

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it selfishly

indicators.note: holding means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: scores, as in many twenties, means many

explanation.surface: Someone tallies points while hosting a midwinter party.
explanation.walkthrough: HOGMANAY is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's New Year's Eve festivities fall on the last night of December.

clue.text: On which every item should be erased!

definitions.text: On which every item should be erased!

parts.words: On which every item should be erased!
parts.note: a list of targets for murder; each name is to be rubbed out, a slang word for killing

explanation.surface: A to-do list where every task is meant to be crossed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erased' here is gangster slang for killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangland slang names a list of people marked for killing.

clue.text: Story: epilogue on stage

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
an epilogue comes at the end

explanation.surface: A tale is given a closing speech in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, such as one about King Arthur.

clue.text: Enjoy one short story about various figures?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for enjoying it
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone relishes a brief anecdote involving several people.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital means expressed in or relating to numbers, so concerned with numerals.

clue.text: Taking refuge initially in damp church, villain

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the damp word

parts.note: wet means damp

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of refuge

explanation.surface: A villain shelters from the rain in a soggy church.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a contemptible scoundrel, a rogue.

clue.text: Cheers echoed for so long

indicators.note: echoed means the word is said once and then again

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

explanation.surface: A toast rings out to mark a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, as is 'cheers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like 'so long'.

clue.text: With sovereign to invest, finding banking system

indicators.note: to invest here means to put something into, so the monarch goes inside

parts.note: tracing someone is finding them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen as sovereign

explanation.surface: A monarch puts money into a bank, uncovering a financial system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' looks financial but means banks of earth or steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracing is a series of stepped banks cut into a hillside or stadium.

clue.text: Relative is not liking angora, woolly tops

indicators.note: tops, in a down answer, means the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A family member dislikes fluffy angora jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relation by marriage, as a mother-in-law is.

clue.text: Struggle with wife in scene

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: A spouse is in a fight during a public row.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a scene or vista seen from a vantage point.

clue.text: Record — I seem disturbed by it

indicators.note: by means the two pieces are placed side by side
disturbed means the letters of I seem are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a record unsettles them.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list or record things one by one.

clue.text: Small group allowed on tour

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a trip is a tour or journey
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A few people are permitted to go on an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is a set of three, a small group.

clue.text: With north winds, east drier? Give up!

indicators.note: winds, as in twists, means the letters of with north are turned about

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a towel is something that dries you

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: northerly winds will make the east drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' reads as weather but is the anagram signal, turning WITH NORTH into THROWINTH. The idiom comes from boxing, where a cornerman concedes by throwing a towel into the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to concede defeat, from a boxer's corner signalling surrender.
